name: time-gradient-every-delivery
description: The long-ladder arm: a bonus on EVERY delivery to a level rather than on the first seats+1 of them, so nothing at the level is ever un-raced. Twice the shipped queue length, since a slot takes two deliveries. This is the far end of the length question the shipped [3,2,1] / [3,2,2,1] / [3,3,2,2,1] leaves open - if even this arm moves no behavioural metric, the length is not the reason the gradient is inert and the cause is elsewhere. Values taper to 1 rather than to 0 on purpose: the question is whether a longer slope bites, not whether a steeper one does. ANSWERED, n=500, 2026-08-08: it does not. Barn at game end 4.5, game length 22 rounds, unfinished games 2.0% and all fourteen assertions identical to the baseline, with only the winning score moving (+4). Length is therefore NOT why the time gradient is inert against the bots, and no ladder is worth sweeping further. The cause is affordability - the bots cannot deliver, so paying them more to deliver early changes nothing - and the next useful run is this arm re-measured AFTER something makes deliveries easier to afford.
